correctness.rationale: The simplex minimization is an exact scalar quadratic calculation. It gives \(\beta_k=\rho_k/(2c^2+\rho_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k(1-\beta_k/\sigma_k)\), and \(\sigma_{k+1}=\sigma_k+\beta_k^2x_k^2/\sigma_k\). With \(\sigma_0\ge1\), every state factor is strictly between zero and one. Since \(\sum_k\beta_k/\sigma_k<\infty\), the infinite product is positive, proving \(x_\infty\ne0\). The displacement and parameter bounds follow by summing exact increments.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural selection question created by the source design: whether a unique Tikhonov-regularized multiplier induces a preferred Pareto point. On the simplest non-singleton symmetric Pareto set, summability gives finite total selection pressure; the exact displacement bound shows that a legal schedule can retain arbitrarily strong initialization bias. This distinguishes multiplier uniqueness from solution selection and is useful for interpreting or redesigning vanishing regularization.
